prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters, simple rounded people with big round eyes, small dot pupils and overbites, flat colour and black outlines everywhere except the faces, which are rendered with startling real skin: pores, stubble, sweat, tired wet eyes. Every flat colour is laid on with thick visible oil brushstrokes. Only the bodies, clothes and places are cartoon: every face in the frame, however small, is painted as real human skin with wrinkles, pores, bags under the eyes and real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, and no feature is exaggerated. Looking straight down from an iron fire escape high above a narrow back alley at dawn, the black iron railing crossing the near foreground: far below, on the back step of a 1930s bakery, a heavy-set Black baker in his fifties with a shaved head, a broken nose and a round double chin, in a floury sweat-stained vest, has stopped dead, his face turned up towards us, staring at his open palm: three small copper coins and a dusty grey moth on it, a torn brown paper pay packet in his other hand. A thin white foreman in a waistcoat walks away up the alley, long dawn shadows on the wet cobbles, dustbins, a warm orange wedge of light from the open bakery door. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
